study type: Prospective observational study with a retrospective component
outcome: Maternal outcomes (abortion, pain, prelabor rupture of membranes (PROM), malpresentation, preterm labor, mode of delivery, postpartum complications)
cohort: The study included 131 pregnant women diagnosed with fibroids antenatally on ultrasound out of 11,383 women who delivered over a two-year period.
finding: Fibroids complicate pregnancy in 8.69% of cases, often asymptomatic, but can lead to complications such as abortion (especially with submucosal fibroids), PROM, malpresentation, and preterm labor, and are associated with both fibroid-related and obstetric indications for cesarean section.
mod_finding: Out of 113 deliveries, 41 (36.3%) were vaginal deliveries and 72 (63.7%) were cesarean sections, with 35 cesarean sections due to fibroid-related indications and 37 due to obstetric indications.
birth_weight: 76% of babies weighed more than 2.5 kg
